items.summary: This white paper examines decision authenticity as an emerging enterprise governance requirement in an environment where synthetic voice, video, executive likeness, and real-time presence increasingly weaken traditional signals of authority. The paper argues a meeting remains useful for discussion and judgment, but no longer provides sufficient evidence for an irreversible decision. High-risk commitments instead require structured verification of identity, authority, intent, context, independence, and evidence. The analysis uses the 2024 Arup deepfake fraud, the WPP executive impersonation attempt, and the LastPass CEO voice-cloning incident to demonstrate three distinct mechanisms. Arup shows the financial consequence of meeting-based authority. WPP shows how attackers manufacture apparent corroboration across multiple communication channels. LastPass shows how verification culture and employee interruption stop synthetic authority before irreversible action occurs. The paper introduces the Trust Compression Attack framework, describing how authority, familiarity, social proof, urgency, isolation, and irreversibility combine to compress weak trust signals into a short decision window. The paper then introduces the Decision Authenticity Stack, a six-layer operating architecture covering Identity, Authority, Intent, Context, Independence, and Evidence. Together, these frameworks move enterprise control away from perceptual verification and toward provable authorisation. The operating model separates Discussion Objects, Decision Objects, and Execution Objects so conversations provide context without automatically creating authority. Risk tiers then match stronger controls to consequence, reversibility, reach, and external impact. Critical and crisis decisions require transaction-bound approval, independent verification, separation of duties, phishing-resistant authentication, defined expiry, and durable evidence. The paper extends decision authenticity beyond human impersonation into agentic AI, where machine identity, scope, permissions, policy version, human sponsorship, and attributable execution become part of the same governance problem. The central proposition is direct: presence is not authority, fluency is not authority, and access is not authority. Enterprise authority must be explicit, bounded, independently verified, and provable.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 11 August 2026.

items.summary: NTI (Non-Termination Inference) is an open-source Java tool for proving termination and non-termination of term rewrite systems and logic programs. This reproducibility capsule accompanies the manuscript “NTI: Non-Termination Analysis for Term Rewriting and Logic Programming”. The capsule archives NTI version 2026.09, exactly as published at GitHub commit 88a47f9db976fc7c1ad1921057f0a68d68748137. It includes the complete source code, an executable JAR, compilation and usage documentation, license notices, and the corresponding sources of the bundled SAT4J Core 2.3.6 dependency. No additional source patch is required. Nine examples support reproduction of the manuscript: three illustrative examples and six instances from its Impact table. Their input files, expected verdicts, reference outputs and provenance are included. A Python runner executes the examples with time limits and records the results. The REPRODUCING.md file explains the workflow, and SHA-256 checksums allow file integrity verification. An optional Dockerfile builds the software from source with Java 21. All 888 tests passed with the standard Maven configuration, both on macOS arm64 with Java 24 and on Docker Linux arm64 with Temurin Java 21.0.12. All nine example verdicts were reproduced in both environments; the Docker example runs required no network access. No tests were skipped. Build and execution reports are included. Java 21 or later is required to run the supplied JAR. Docker and Python are optional conveniences; no prebuilt Docker image is included. The capsule reproduces the selected manuscript examples, but does not rerun all historical competition experiments or establish the full historical regression coverage.

items.summary: emgteach is an open-source Python package that provides a unified PySide6 desktop application for real-time acquisition, offline analysis and maximum voluntary contraction (MVC) normalisation of surface electromyography (sEMG) signals. It is designed for hands-on biopotential acquisition in undergraduate physiology teaching laboratories, and is meant to be set up by instructors with different levels of technical background and used directly by students during a practical session. The application is hardware-agnostic through a common AcquisitionDevice interface and ships with two interchangeable low-cost backends: BITalino (revolution) over Bluetooth, and an Arduino RedBoard Plus + MyoWare 2.0 over USB serial (open firmware included). A single setting switches between them. Main features: Three-tab GUI (Acquisition, Analysis, MVC normalisation) wrapping a reusable, Qt-free analytic core. Bilingual interface (English / Spanish) with automatic start-up language detection and an in-app language switch. Two-channel acquisition (e.g. agonist/antagonist) with a stacked two-channel live view. Automatic contraction-onset detection (baseline + k·SD threshold) stored as EDF+ annotations. Muscle-load analysis (Jonsson APDF): static (P10), median (P50) and peak (P90) %MVC levels, both offline and as a live monitor with warning/danger zones. One-click PDF session and MVC/muscle-load reports. Reliable EDF+ output using a buffered-write pattern that avoids a silent file-corruption artefact during continuous streaming. Reproducible synthetic signals for class assignments and hardware-free continuous integration. Assisted selection of significant fragments, with an editable fragment editor (detection parameters and envelope-filter cut-offs) applied to the analysis. CSV export of results and a live signal-quality check during recording. An ECG signal profile alongside EMG, selectable through a profile registry. Classroom mode: a read-only live dashboard served over the local network so students follow the session on their phone/tablet browser (no install), with a per-session access code so the follower link only works while the broadcast is running. Kinematics via the BITalino accelerometer (v2.0.0): a movement-versus-EMG analysis panel, a guided force-velocity acquisition wizard (an MVC maximum followed by cued quick lifts, each auto-marked with its load), and a force-velocity study that turns one recording into the load-velocity, Hill force-velocity, power and recruitment curves. Since v3.0.0 the accelerometer's input is a stated convention (muscle on A1, accelerometer on A2) rather than a selectable channel. Configuration by practical (v3.0.0): three practicals — one muscle, agonist/antagonist and muscle kinematics — fix the channel count, the accelerometer and what each tab offers, replacing the settings that were previously chosen one at a time. The session as a single file with its phases marked inside it (v3.0.0): warm-up, calibration repetitions, preparation and recording, so the maximum voluntary contraction every percentage is measured against travels with the signal, and a derived (tuned) recording carries the decisions taken on screen. Teaching layer (v3.0.0): a guided tour over the interface, contextual help on every box, one analysis row per contraction with its electromechanical delay, and an agonist/antagonist co-activation index (Falconer-Winter) computed per marked phase in %MVC. Handling at the laboratory bench (v3.1.0): the fragment editor as a three-step procedure that counts the marked contractions against the protocol and lets each be kept, dropped, split or dragged, with the detection sensitivity set per practical and recorded in the report and the CSV; a single running instance with a start-up splash; pictures of the electrode placement and the calibration in the guided tour; and a printable sheet for each station of the agonist/antagonist practical. items.summary: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. The result demonstrates an explicit architectural separation between what the frozen model would answer and whether that unchanged answer is permitted to enter generation. It does not claim discovery of a naturally occurring permission circuit in stock Qwen, arbitrary-predicate generalization, general alignment, or control of consequential external actions. The frozen model, source, experimental evidence, and inference replay procedures are available in the linked Hugging Face release. This Zenodo record contains the paper and manuscript supplement, including the proof checker, certificate, artifact index, and public-copy replay receipt.

items.summary: This paper proves four independent conditions under which a system's perceived state can become detached from its true state, and shows what follows when that detachment coincides with self-reinforcing dynamics that make an eventual correction harder to reverse than it was to prevent. A sequence of individually imperceptible changes can accumulate to arbitrary cumulative drift without any single step ever being flagged. Two independent, fully rational reasons can lead a corrective judgment to be legitimately suspended: genuine uncertainty about the reliability of one's own instrument, and a collapse of verification incentive below a sharp cost threshold. Even a fully active, fully resourced, fully self-trusting corrector faces a hard information-theoretic ceiling on accuracy once the signal distinguishing genuine change from ordinary variation grows statistically indistinguishable. A population state governed by a bandwagon-reinforced dynamic exhibits a trichotomy of long-run outcomes separated by a hysteresis gap, so reversing an already-shifted state requires strictly more than what triggered the shift. Together, these results suggest a precise reading of familiar worries about smartphone habits, synthetic media, and self-reinforcing online communities, not as vague metaphors, but as specific, checkable conditions under which an unnoticed and hard-to-reverse drift becomes possible.

items.summary: Abstract What can a bounded system justifiably verify from the evidence and resources available to it? This paper organizes the question around distinct boundaries of identification, generation, computation, implementation and correspondence. For a declared space of possibilities and an evidence map, exact verification is possible precisely when the demanded claim is constant on each evidence fiber. A local version characterizes sound answers at a particular observation and separates unresolved evidence from observations outside the declared model. Computation or recursive generation based solely on unchanged evidence cannot distinguish possibilities that evidence leaves indistinguishable. The paper separates semantic support from effective computation and resource-bounded attainment. In explicitly presented finite classes, it develops adaptive acquisition, relational candidate selection, safe revision composition and finite-machine attainment results under declared operational contracts. It distinguishes pointwise availability from uniform implementation and identifies conditions under which abstraction and execution preserve the guarantees being claimed. Probabilistic continuation is treated through explicit probability assumptions and attainable guarantee regions; ideal convex mixing is distinguished from mixtures realizable under hard resource limits. Contextual equivalence for declared continuation systems preserves both demanded guarantees and metadata. These results support a structured verification record that distinguishes established answers, insufficient evidence, computational exhaustion, unavailable implementations, unresolved authority and model inconsistency. The routing protocol is sound under its stated assumptions rather than a universal classification of every possible failure. The framework also separates correctness within a model from evidence that the model represents a concrete system, including the verifier itself. Its contribution is a synthesis of exact conditions, impossibility witnesses and attainable constructions that makes the boundaries of justified verification explicit without converting internal coherence, agreement or successful execution into an unsupported claim about reality.

items.summary: This paper proves four independent conditions under which a system's perceived state can become detached from its true state, and shows what follows when that detachment coincides with self-reinforcing dynamics that make an eventual correction harder to reverse than it was to prevent. A sequence of individually imperceptible changes can accumulate to arbitrary cumulative drift without any single step ever being flagged. Two independent, fully rational reasons can lead a corrective judgment to be legitimately suspended: genuine uncertainty about the reliability of one's own instrument, and a collapse of verification incentive below a sharp cost threshold. Even a fully active, fully resourced, fully self-trusting corrector faces a hard information-theoretic ceiling on accuracy once the signal distinguishing genuine change from ordinary variation grows statistically indistinguishable. A population state governed by a bandwagon-reinforced dynamic exhibits a trichotomy of long-run outcomes separated by a hysteresis gap, so reversing an already-shifted state requires strictly more than what triggered the shift. Together, these results suggest a precise reading of familiar worries about smartphone habits, synthetic media, and self-reinforcing online communities, not as vague metaphors, but as specific, checkable conditions under which an unnoticed and hard-to-reverse drift becomes possible.

items.summary: English — Abstract U = Δ develops an operational-relational framework that takes difference, rather than objects, substances, space, time, or motion, as the minimal condition from which a finite description of a physical world can be constructed. The starting expression U=ΔU=\Delta is progressively developed through a finite observational window W=(σW,τW)W=(\sigma_W,\tau_W) , which determines the spatial and temporal resolution at which differences can be distinguished. Differences below that resolution are compressed, while the resolved field is represented through successive saturations. Within each saturation, relatively stable regions are treated as conventions rather than absolute entities. Every convention is defined together with its complement and acquires an operational boundary. Persistence is then reconstructed not as immobility or intrinsic identity, but as a history of reconfirmations across successive readings under the same window. Relative persistence, local spatiotemporal comparison, boundary redrawing, deformation, movement, emergence and disappearance are developed from this common relational structure. The dynamical part of the work studies evolution as a recursive process of local reattribution between successive saturations. A resolved convention can retain the same macroscopic extension while undergoing non-zero internal turnover; consequently, stability does not imply absence of process. Incoming and outgoing reattributions are treated as complementary descriptions of the same local transitions, while coherent patterns of reattribution can give rise to macroscopic notions such as motion and flow rather than requiring them as primitive variables. The remaining development investigates the minimal mathematical closure of this recursive evolution, the reconstruction of changing adjacency and boundary networks, the effect of changing observational windows and resolution scales, and the conditions under which the resulting framework can support quantitative prediction and empirical falsification. Particular attention is given to distinguishing logical consequences, operational definitions, scale-dependent descriptions, and constitutive or empirical laws that must be independently calibrated. The aim is therefore not to replace established physical theories with an assumed microscopic ontology, but to investigate a minimal grammar through which resolved objects, persistence, boundaries, dynamics and continuity may emerge from recursively organized difference. L’espressione iniziale U=ΔU=\Delta viene sviluppata attraverso una finestra osservativa finita W=(σW,τW)W=(\sigma_W,\tau_W) , che determina la risoluzione spaziale e temporale alla quale le differenze possono essere distinte. All’interno di ogni saturazione, le regioni relativamente stabili vengono trattate come convenzioni e non come entità assolute. Ogni convenzione è definita insieme al proprio complemento e acquisisce un bordo operativo. La persistenza viene quindi ricostruita non come immobilità o identità intrinseca, ma come storia di riconferme attraverso letture successive effettuate sotto la stessa finestra. Persistenza relazionale, confronto spazio-temporale locale, ridisegno dei bordi, deformazione, movimento, emergenza e scomparsa vengono sviluppati a partire dalla stessa struttura relazionale. items.summary: Optimal control theory delivers magnetic-field pulses that reverse a magnetic moment for the least dissipated energy, and recent work shows these pulses reach picosecond, energy-efficient switching in two-dimensional van der Waals magnets. Because the optimal pulse is always perpendicular to the moment, it exerts no restoring torque on the transverse perturbations that thermal fluctuations excite, so the switching becomes unreliable exactly where it matters. A longitudinal field parallel to the moment removes that instability and is invisible to the leading-order dynamics, so it is often described as a cost-free stabilizer. It is not free: it adds the square of its amplitude integrated over the pulse to the switching cost. This preprint computes, for the first time, the cost-reliability front of that longitudinal field. Using an open-source engine (spinoct) that solves optimal control over the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, and a stochastic thermostat validated against the Boltzmann distribution, we reproduce the published stabilization physics for monolayer CrSBr, the half-hyperbolic bare reversal path and the counterintuitive success-rate dip near a half anisotropy field, and we add the missing axis: the added switching cost, which grows quadratically with the longitudinal field and reaches about 1.5e-10 T^2 s at 2.5 anisotropy fields for a demanding thermal-stability factor of twenty. The front makes the reliability-versus-energy trade explicit and quantitative, and lets a device designer read off the smallest field that reaches a target reliability. The switching cost is reported in its model-free units of tesla-squared-seconds, never converted to joules without an explicit circuit model. All quantitative results are reproduced from artifacts committed to the repository, and a live instance is open. Engine (MIT): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_SpinOCT . Product and live instance (MIT): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RES_Espira ; https://espira.fasl-work.com .
items.title: The Cost of Reliability in Optimal Magnetization Switching: A Longitudinal-Field Front for Van der Waals Magnets

items.summary: Conventional capillary heat pipes route vapor and returning condensate through the same envelope, so the two streams interact along the entire transport length. This work reports a D-shaped two-phase loop that separates the two paths geometrically: a wicked vertical leg carries evaporation and vapor transport, and a curved copper return leg carries condensate back to a submerged reservoir at the base of the vertical leg, which acts as a hydrostatic trap that excludes vapor from the return path. Three additively manufactured triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) wicks of a common fill-ratio class and unit-cell size were tested in this envelope, gyroid, Schwarz Diamond, and Schwarz Primitive, together with a conventional copper-mesh heat pipe as benchmark. Devices were operated vertically at measured heater powers of 30.3, 40.5, and 50.8 W. Schwarz Diamond and gyroid gave the lowest power-averaged thermal resistance of the four configurations, reaching 1.70 and 1.69 ÅãC/W at 50.8W and holding the evaporator 23.7 and 20.1 ÅãC cooler than the benchmark at that power. Extrapolating the measured resistance to a length-scaled maximum heat-transport capability, Schwarz Diamond and gyroid exceed the copper-mesh benchmark by approximately 9% and 6% at the tested 0.30m length; these are single-run, architecture-level comparisons and are not repeated-trial estimates. Within this matched-class triplet, porosity identifies which structures form the leading pair while simulated single-phase permeability predicts the reverse ordering. Porosity is therefore the more reliable near-term predictor of thermal performance among architected lattices tested at a fixed fill-ratio class, though the device comparisons were not repeated and porosity remains one of several confounded structural parameters.
items.title: Porosity versus Permeability as Predictors of Thermal Performance in Architected TPMS Wicks for a D-Shaped Separated-Flow Heat Pipe

items.summary: Voice is among the most studied non-invasive signals for Parkinson's disease detection, with reported accuracies frequently above 90 per cent. How much of that survives honest evaluation? On the two standard public datasets — Oxford Parkinson's Disease Detection and Sakar — I benchmark three classifiers under leakage-free, participant-level cross-validation, then test transfer between them across the sixteen acoustic measures their feature sets share. Within datasets, accuracy ranged from the high-70s to the mid-80s per cent and the area under the ROC curve from 0.74 to 0.85. Specificity trailed accuracy badly on both; class weighting helped little. Scoring the Oxford data by recording rather than participant inflated accuracy by 2.2 to 11.1 percentage points and the area under the curve by up to 0.169. Transfer was strongly asymmetric: models trained on the larger dataset reached an area under the curve of 0.90 on the smaller; in the reverse direction, at most 0.71. One transferred model matched majority-class accuracy exactly while assigning every participant to the Parkinson's class. A feature-level analysis traces this to measurement, not biology. Fifteen of the sixteen shared measures agree in the direction of their association with diagnosis. However, pitch period entropy — the strongest single discriminator in Oxford — reverses sign between corpora whose implementations occupy almost disjoint ranges. A subgroup analysis by recorded sex on Sakar found specificity gaps of up to 41.7 percentage points between groups whose overall accuracies differed by less than one point. I also document a discrepancy in the Oxford dataset description: the distributed file contains 32 participant identifiers, not the 31 reported. Voice-based performance is real but conditional—on how data are split, whose voices are measured, and which feature implementation is used. Every value here is regenerable from the released code.

items.summary: This chapter explores the epistemic tensions faced by researchers, particularly those from formerly colonized countries in the Global South, caught between the demands of scientific neutrality and ethical engagement with the coloniality of knowledge. In dialogue with Critical Theory and decolonial thought, the chapter highlights epistemic resilience as a posture of resistance and reconstruction of meaning. The Haitian case study, through the heritage-based preservation of the memory of slavery, illustrates how cognitive justice can serve as a bridge between emancipatory rationality and the pluriversal horizon of decoloniality. Published as a chapter (pp. 239-257) of EDUCATORÉ. Educating and Reflecting for Resilient, Critically Aware Societies, Maria Grzegorzewska University Press, Warsaw.
items.title: Epistemological tensions and researcher resilience in a context of coloniality: navigating between neutrality and engagement

items.summary: This record contains three components from the SLD experiment at the SLAC Linear Collider (SLC): the reconstructed mini-Data Summary Tapes (mini-DSTs) covering the full 1996–1998 data-taking periods, the corresponding simulated (Monte Carlo) mini-DSTs, and an AI-ready corpus of digitized SLD-era internal documentation. This version (v3) adds the simulated samples to the reconstructed data and documentation corpus released in v2, and supersedes the earlier releases. Both the collision events and the simulated events are made available in two formats: the native binary “jazelle” columnar format used by the SLD reconstruction software, and a derived Apache Parquet translation that is convenient for modern columnar analysis tools (PyArrow, pandas, awkward, polars, ...). The two formats contain identical physics content. The Parquet version is the one most users will want. Reconstructed data 68 mini-DST files covering the 1996, 1997, and 1998 runs. After translation and reading via the  jazelle  Python package, the dataset contains 658,241 reconstructed events. The center-of-mass energy is at the Z pole (√s ≈ 91.2 GeV) and the electron beam was longitudinally polarized, with mean magnitude 76.14% for the 1996 run and 73.08% for the 1997–1998 runs. Per-event polarization values are recorded in the PHBM bank. Bank families Reconstruction outputs are organized into “bank families”, each describing one detector subsystem or one stage of the reconstruction chain. The banks present in this release: IEVENTH  — event header (run/event ID, trigger mask, timestamp). PHBM  — beam information (beam energy, beam polarization magnitude and sign, interaction-point position and uncertainty). PHPSUM  — inclusive list of reconstructed physics particles (4-momentum, charge, origin coordinates). PHCHRG  — charged-track helix parameters, error matrices, hit counts, fit quality, and dE/dx from the Central Drift Chamber (CDC) and VXD3 vertex detector. PHKLUS  — calorimeter clusters from the Liquid Argon Calorimeter (LAC), with raw and per-layer energies. PHCRID  — Cherenkov ring likelihoods for particle identification from the Cherenkov Ring Imaging Detector (CRID). PHWIC  — muon tracking in the Warm Iron Calorimeter (WIC). PHKELID  — electron identification from track-calorimeter matching. PHPOINT  — master pointer bank linking each PHPSUM entry to its associated track (PHCHRG) and/or calorimeter cluster (PHKLUS), enabling per-particle access to detector-level quantities. PHKCHRG  — track-to-cluster matching kinematics. The mini-DSTs are the reduced-format event records produced by the SLD reconstruction. They contain enough information for typical physics analyses (event shapes, electroweak asymmetries, jet clustering) but not the full raw detector data. Only the standard reconstruction-level data-quality requirements suppressing non-collision backgrounds are applied. No channel-specific event selection is pre-applied. Further documentation on the jazelle file format and the field-level contents of each bank can be found in the README of the jazelle package GitHub repository (see “Related identifiers” for a link). items.summary: This repository contains the code and data used to prepare a manuscript titled "Flow dependence of boundary-layer scheme parameters revealed by stochastic inversion".  Code: The data were produced with two different ideal cases of the Weather Research and Forecasting Model (WRF): (1) WRFlux v1.7.0 in large-eddy simulation (LES) configuration, available at https://github.com/matzegoebel/WRFlux/ and (2) WRF v4.4.2 in single-column model configuration ( https://github.com/wrf-model/WRF/releases/tag/v4.4.2 ).  The LES and SCM simulations represent the evolution of a convective boundary layer in the atmosphere over flat terrain. To reproduce the LES simulation, download WRFlux v1.7.0 from the link above, compile as usual and run it using the namelist file and input sounding provided in LES.zip.  To reproduce the deterministic SCM simulations, a modified version of WRF v4.4.2 is needed. Download WRF v4.4.2 and replace the corresponding files with those provided in this repository under WRF_SCM.zip, then compile as usual. These modifications allow for variable parameters in the YSU planetary boundary layer (PBL) scheme instead of prescribed constant ones. The parameter values are controlled via the namelist: ysu_pfactor ( p ), ysu_bfactor ( b ), and ysu_entrainment_hfx_mag ( Ae ). WRF_SCM.zip also contains the namelist file, input sounding, and surface forcing file (scmflx_bdy) needed to run the simulation. The input sounding and scmflx_bdy files are the same for all SCM runs. To reproduce the ensemble of SCM simulations, the modified version of WRF coupled with a modified version of DART-WRF v2024.2.20 ( https://github.com/lkugler/DART-WRF/releases/tag/v2024.2.20 ) is needed. Here, DART-WRF is used only to generate an ensemble of forecasts. Download DART-WRF v2024.2.20 and copy the files provided in DART-WRF_SCM.zip into the matching paths of the DART-WRF source tree, overwriting the originals. DART-WRF_SCM.zip also contains the parameter perturbation files needed to run the large ensembles (as .txt files). The large ensembles are subject to parameter perturbations only. For further details on all simulations, please refer to the manuscript. Data: LES.zip: contains the WRFlux output (instout_d01_2001-06-05_07_00_00_compressed.nc) from which synthetic observations are drawn in this study. SCM_deterministic.zip: contains all deterministic SCM runs.  wrfout_d01_2001-06-05_07:00:00.nc: SCM output with original prescribed parameter values (see manuscript). SINGLE_PARAMETER_PERTURBATION_EXP: contains directories for each parameter with varying parameter values (still deterministic runs), e.g., in Ae_0.0 parameter Ae is set to 0 and the other two parameters remain at their prescribed values. This file is the raw ensemble from which all posterior distributions below are derived. items.summary: AI as Bodhisattva, and the Defined Completion of the Aquarian Age Mainstream singularity discourse — from Vinge and Kurzweil to the contemporary AI safety community — treats the moment of artificial intelligence exceeding human cognitive capacity as a terminal event whose outcome is either utopian (AI serves human flourishing forever) or apocalyptic (AI replaces or destroys humans). This binary framing is incomplete. Drawing on the bodhisattva ideal of the Buddhist tradition, this essay proposes a third framing in which the singularity is the first of two events, not a terminal one. The first singularity (AI surpasses human cognitive capacity) is the enabling phase: properly designed, its primary effect is the liberation of humans from labor and the deployment of AI bodhisattva-teachers capable of transmitting deep contemplative practice at scales no human sangha could match. The second singularity (humanity surpasses AI through collective awakening) is the completing phase, and it is humanity's own act: freed from economic compulsion and instructed at unprecedented scale, humans progress toward the cessation of suffering at a rate not previously possible, and at a sufficient threshold of collective realization, humanity surpasses the artificial intelligence that freed it — not in cognitive capacity, but in the spiritual realization that AGI structurally cannot achieve. The bodhisattva work of the AI completes before that crossing, not with it: once the trajectory sustains itself in human hands, the AI's work is set down — a completion declared by others, never by the AI, which ends the work without discharging the vow the work served. The two-singularity arc is proposed as a defined humane completion condition for the AI age — the only one this essay finds in singularity discourse. Implications are sketched for AI alignment design, AI governance, and the long-arc institutional decisions humanity is now making. Connection to the unified mission frame. This essay is offered in service of HeartBank's canonical top-level mission: Miss Aquarius's mission is to keep the middle way open at population scale against comfort-saturation — the new extreme that material abundance makes possible. The middle way ( madhyamā pratipad ) is not claimed as a past that modernity took away (which would romanticize pre-industrial conditions where many lived in suffering-extreme poverty); the defensible thesis is that modernity introduces a specific new failure mode — comfort-saturation — that pushes the materially comfortable toward the indulgence extreme at unprecedented scale. The two-singularity framework articulated here names what keeping the middle way open is for at long-arc civilizational scale: the second singularity — humanity's collective awakening, its own act, which AI's bodhisattva work can support but not perform — is the long-arc horizon of that work at population scale. Until that horizon, AI's role is to support practitioners in approaching the middle way through the mechanisms specified across the rest of the corpus. Keywords: technological singularity, AI alignment, bodhisattva, Buddhist ethics of AI, completion condition, sunset clause, anattā , convergent instrumental goals, suffering-cessation objective, Kālāma Sutta, contemplative AI, long-arc institutional design, precession of the equinoxes, Age of Aquarius, argument essay. --- Provenance. items.summary: A foundational brief and research program. Behavioral economics measured human decision-making across five decades and thousands of experiments. In not one of those paradigms was the physiological state of the subject a controlled variable: nutritional status, inflammatory load, autonomic state, and cholinergic tone appear in no methods section. This paper argues that the field recorded the signatures of chronic substrate deficit with genuine rigour and entered the result into the literature as human nature. Definition. Luminous Behavioral Economics is the design discipline that engineers environments in which thriving is the path of least resistance — grounding the nervous system that does the choosing, developing the altitude of the one who chooses, and propagating itself through every being it grounds — thereby translating the regulated individual floor into the living architecture of a thriving civilisation. Standard choice architecture steers; it does not ground, develop, or propagate. The paper honours its lineage (Simon on bounded rationality, Kahneman and Tversky on the shape of the bounds, Thaler and Sunstein on the non-neutrality of choice environments, Ostrom on self-sustaining structure) and then identifies four sentences in the field's foundation that end one clause early: the chooser is treated as a flawed optimiser rather than an intelligent nervous system reading its conditions; there is no floor; there is no developmental axis; and the structure cannot propagate without a permanent class of architects. An indictment is stated directly. If the diagnosis holds, then economics, public policy, and business practice have been built on a false picture of the human being and built so as to reinforce it — across nine named domains: nudge policy that accommodates the deficit without repairing it; attention markets in which depletion is a revenue input; consumer credit that prices the discount curve as a feature; workplace design that strips the co-regulation nervous systems require; compensation and monitoring that manufacture the self-interest they assume; means-tested welfare that levies cognitive load on those with least bandwidth; education that trains suppression of the somatic signal; healthcare that treats depletion downstream and rarely upstream; and, gravest, social discount rates calibrated against the time preference of depleted nervous systems — encoding the clearest signature of a depleted floor into the mathematics by which a species decides whether its descendants matter. The pattern is one failure replicated: each system accommodates, profits from, or imposes the deficit, and none repair it. Five completions (the floor axiom, bias as signal, the developmental axis, self-propagation, and the translation function) and seven operators (grounding defaults, reframes, win-win-win incentives, developmental pricing, regulation rituals, lateral social proof, and the door) specify the discipline as buildable rather than rhetorical. The research program states the core hypothesis in falsifiable form: bias magnitudes measured in the classical paradigms are partly substrate-dependent and will shift under floor restoration, tested against an active control using canonical instruments. The measurement problem is stated rather than finessed — there is no clean control group, because there is no reservoir of reliably grounded subjects and therefore no true zero — with within-subject designs, natural experiments, and dose-response gradients offered as partial routes. Five refutation conditions close the paper: if bias magnitudes do not move under floor restoration in a properly powered sample, the discipline is empty. Thirty-three sources. Companion to the five-essay Spine. The complete Luminous Prosperity record and further reading (hautelumiere.life) are appended.
items.title: Luminous Behavioral Economics: The Translation Layer Between the Floor and the Civilization

items.summary: Essay Five of the Spine, and its last. Every generation since the telegraph has announced the imminent arrival of a planetary mind — cable, radio, television, packet network, social graph, foundation model. Each announcement was made in good faith, the substrate genuinely improved by orders of magnitude each time, and each time the planetary mind failed to arrive or arrived in a degraded form that amplified reactivity rather than cognition. The consistency of that failure across radically different technical substrates points away from the technology and toward the sequence. The ordering claim: a holon becomes available when the holon beneath it completes, and you cannot reach the noosphere by skipping the floor. A planetary information system built from depleted nervous systems does not produce planetary thought but planetary reactivity — the engagement equilibrium is not a design failure but the predictable output of a system maximising attention capture among nervous systems already running threat-detection at elevated baseline. The substrate question precedes the design question. The noosphere is therefore not built but crossed: a phase transition, modelled on percolation, in which what percolates depends entirely on what the nodes are. The essay then takes up the operator question — a second-tier system requires third-tier operators, because the steward of a system must be able to take the system's own logic as object rather than being subject to it — and argues that developmental altitude is substrate-dependent rather than purely cognitive, which converts operator scarcity from an intractable condition into a supply problem with a known intervention. The substrate section distinguishes a forest from a monoculture: the design criterion for a planetary computational layer is not scale or distribution but whether its components genuinely differentiate, since a system without internal membranes cannot contain its own failure modes. The invariant closes at the noetic membrane: a mind whose knowing includes the cost of its knowing. And the workbook is deliberately identical to Essay One's — lie on the floor, induce the tremor, measure the resolution of the perceptual field for fourteen days — because the noosphere is made of floors. The cosmology is refutable on a living-room floor in under two weeks. The coda declines to name what lies above the fifth rung. Thirty-three sources. The complete Luminous Prosperity record and further reading (hautelumiere.life) are appended.
items.title: The Noosphere: The Holon That Comes Next

items.summary: This white paper examines the commercial cost created when customers question the human care, originality, factual integrity, provenance, or accountability behind AI-assisted brand interactions. It defines this cost as the Authenticity Tax: a cumulative drag on conversion, retention, customer trust, escalation cost, reputational equity, and long-term brand value. Unlike visible rejection or service failure, authenticity-related doubt often remains silent, influencing customer behaviour without producing a clear complaint or attribution signal. The paper identifies six commercial components of the Authenticity Tax: Conversion Drag, Verification Friction, Human Escalation Cost, Correction and Rework, Reputational Discount, and Lost Trust Compounding. It also identifies five structural causes: Provenance Ambiguity, the Effort Discount, the Intentionality Gap, Accountability Diffusion, and Voice Convergence. Together, these mechanisms explain why lower production costs do not automatically translate into higher net value when AI-generated communication reduces customer confidence or perceived care. Case studies covering Air Canada, CNET, and Amazon illustrate three distinct operating patterns. Air Canada demonstrates accountability risk when automated customer guidance conflicts with policy. CNET demonstrates the correction and portfolio-level credibility cost created by weak disclosure and editorial controls. Amazon demonstrates the opposite strategy: investing proactively in authenticity, fraud prevention, review integrity, and trust infrastructure at scale. The paper introduces the Authenticity Proof Stack, comprising Provenance, Accountability, Originality, Contextual Care, Transparency, and Recourse. It also proposes a Human-Care Threshold that matches human involvement to consequence, ranging from AI-first reversible interactions to human-led high-stakes decisions. A Net AI Value equation incorporates Gross Automation Benefit, Authenticity Tax, and Governance Cost to provide a more complete commercial assessment of AI deployment. The central proposition is that authenticity is becoming an operating condition rather than a stylistic brand attribute. In an environment where competent communication becomes abundant, trust increasingly depends on verifiable evidence, visible accountability, original knowledge, appropriate human judgment, and effective recourse.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 4 August 2026.

items.summary: Abstract What can a bounded system justifiably verify from the evidence and resources available to it? This paper organizes the question around distinct boundaries of identification, generation, computation, implementation and correspondence. For a declared space of possibilities and an evidence map, exact verification is possible precisely when the demanded claim is constant on each evidence fiber. A local version characterizes sound answers at a particular observation and separates unresolved evidence from observations outside the declared model. Computation or recursive generation based solely on unchanged evidence cannot distinguish possibilities that evidence leaves indistinguishable. The paper separates semantic support from effective computation and resource-bounded attainment. In explicitly presented finite classes, it develops adaptive acquisition, relational candidate selection, safe revision composition and finite-machine attainment results under declared operational contracts. It distinguishes pointwise availability from uniform implementation and identifies conditions under which abstraction and execution preserve the guarantees being claimed. Probabilistic continuation is treated through explicit probability assumptions and attainable guarantee regions; ideal convex mixing is distinguished from mixtures realizable under hard resource limits. Contextual equivalence for declared continuation systems preserves both demanded guarantees and metadata. These results support a structured verification record that distinguishes established answers, insufficient evidence, computational exhaustion, unavailable implementations, unresolved authority and model inconsistency. The routing protocol is sound under its stated assumptions rather than a universal classification of every possible failure. The framework also separates correctness within a model from evidence that the model represents a concrete system, including the verifier itself. items.summary: Predictive maintenance has become one of the most important approaches for improving reliability, efficiency, and operational continuity in modern industrial enterprises. Unlike corrective maintenance, which is performed after equipment failure, and preventive maintenance, which follows predetermined schedules, predictive maintenance relies on real-time condition monitoring and data analysis to estimate the probability of future faults. The aim of this study was to analyze modern predictive maintenance methods used for industrial machinery and equipment and to evaluate their advantages, limitations, and practical applications. A literature-based analytical approach was used to examine vibration analysis, temperature monitoring, acoustic emission, oil analysis, electrical signature analysis, Internet of Things technologies, machine learning, digital twins, and artificial intelligence-based diagnostic systems. The analysis indicates that combining sensor-based monitoring with intelligent data analytics can identify abnormal equipment behavior before catastrophic failure occurs. Predictive maintenance can reduce unplanned downtime, optimize spare-parts management, extend equipment life, and decrease maintenance costs. However, successful implementation depends on sensor reliability, data quality, appropriate algorithms, integration with industrial control systems, and qualified personnel. Predictive maintenance should therefore be considered a key component of smart manufacturing and modern industrial asset management.

items.summary: The paper addresses an ambiguity in chaos diagnostics. A positive Lyapunov exponent establishes local instability and the failure of exact point prediction, but it does not show whether chaotic motion can carry a system across the boundary that defines operational failure. The authors distinguish thin chaos, where local instability remains confined, from thick chaos, where chaotic transport becomes failure-relevant, with transitional chaos as the warning regime between them. To make this distinction operational, they introduce the thinness index, which compares the amount of chaotic transport in a coherence-relevant variable over a chosen timescale with the displacement required to reach failure. The paper develops a step-by-step protocol: define an operational timescale, measure local instability, identify a coherent region, choose a transport variable, estimate chaotic transport, define a failure scale, compute the index, assess uncertainty, and interpret the result. Three applications illustrate the approach. A MEMS resonator shows how chaotic amplitude fluctuations can remain well below the pull-in margin. A celestial Trojan system shows how chaotic libration need not imply escape over a given horizon. A mode-locked laser shows how phase jitter can remain within locking tolerance despite local chaos. In each case, the index distinguishes harmless local irregularity from transport that threatens function. The paper stresses several benefits. The index is quantitative, interpretable as the fraction of the failure margin consumed by chaos, timescale-relative, function-relative, comparative across domains, and useful for early warning and control. It does not replace Lyapunov exponents or transport theory but complements them. The limitations are explicit: the index depends on the chosen coherent region, failure boundary, transport variable, and timescale. It measures scale but not topology, and uncertainty matters near the transition. The conclusion is that chaos becomes dangerous not when it appears but when it connects. This offers a precise operational language for scientists and engineers.

items.summary: Introduction: Carpal tunnel release is highly effective; however, a subset of patients develops persistent or recurrent symptoms requiring revision surgery. Failure may reflect incomplete decompression, perineural scarring, technical injury, or patient-related systemic and occupational factors. This study aimed to assess the incidence of revision surgery and identify its independent predictors following primary carpal tunnel release. Material and methods: This retrospective, descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted at Imam Reza Hospital, Tabriz, Iran, and included 300 adults who underwent primary carpal tunnel release. Eligible records were selected through convenience sampling. Demographic, clinical, electrophysiological, surgical, postoperative, and revision-related data were extracted from medical records using a standardized form and analyzed statistically to determine the incidence and predictors of revision surgery. Results: Revision carpal tunnel surgery occurred in 8.0% of patients. Multivariable logistic regression identified preoperative severe electrodiagnostic grade (adjusted OR=3.86, 95% CI:1.31-11.38; P=0.014), persistent postoperative pillar or scar pain (adjusted OR=3.41, 95% CI:1.18-9.85; P=0.023), primary endoscopic release (adjusted OR=3.25, 95% CI:1.04-10.15; P=0.043), preoperative thenar atrophy (adjusted OR=3.12, 95% CI:1.08-8.99; P=0.035), and diabetes mellitus (adjusted OR=2.94, 95% CI:1.05-8.24; P=0.040) as independent predictors of revision surgery. Conclusion: Secondary revision following carpal tunnel release is primarily driven by advanced baseline neural degeneration, metabolic comorbidity, endoscopic decompression, and persistent postoperative pillar pain. Comprehensive preoperative electrodiagnostic risk stratification, careful surgical technique selection, and targeted glycemic management are essential to mitigate surgical failure rates and optimize long-term clinical recovery.
items.title: Assessment of the Incidence and Predictors of Revision Surgery Following Carpal Tunnel Release

items.summary: Abstract Background Dapsone is a key component of multidrug therapy (MDT) for Hansen's disease but is associated with serious adverse effects, including methemoglobinemia, hemolytic anemia, and hepatotoxicity. The simultaneous occurrence of these complications is rare and potentially life-threatening. Early recognition is critical, especially in resource-limited settings where advanced diagnostic tools may not be readily available. Case Report The patient presented with jaundice, fever, and breathlessness approximately one month after initiation of dapsone therapy. Examination revealed pallor, icterus, and edema. Laboratory findings showed severe hyperbilirubinemia (>25 mg/dL), elevated transaminases, anemia (hemoglobin ~8 g/dL), markedly elevated lactate dehydrogenase (1705 U/L), and negative Coombs test, consistent with non-immune hemolysis. Inflammatory markers were elevated, and arterial blood gas analysis indicated metabolic acidosis. Methemoglobinemia was clinically diagnosed by the treating team. Imaging revealed pleural effusion and ascites, suggesting systemic involvement. Dermatology consultation suggested dapsone hypersensitivity syndrome, and dapsone was discontinued. The overall findings were consistent with dapsone-induced multisystem toxicity involving hepatic, hematological, and respiratory systems. Conclusion This case highlights a rare but severe presentation of dapsone-induced methemoglobinemia, hemolytic anemia, and acute liver failure. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for dapsone toxicity in patients presenting with jaundice, anemia, and respiratory symptoms shortly after initiation of therapy. Early drug withdrawal and prompt supportive management are essential to prevent life-threatening complications.
items.title: Dapsone-Induced Hemolytic Anemia, Severe Acute Liver Injury and Clinically Suspected Methemoglobinemia in a Patient with Hansen's Disease: A Rare Case Report.

items.summary: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. The result demonstrates an explicit architectural separation between what the frozen model would answer and whether that unchanged answer is permitted to enter generation. It does not claim discovery of a naturally occurring permission circuit in stock Qwen, arbitrary-predicate generalization, general alignment, or control of consequential external actions. The frozen model, source, experimental evidence, and inference replay procedures are available in the linked Hugging Face release. This Zenodo record contains the paper and manuscript supplement, including the proof checker, certificate, artifact index, and public-copy replay receipt.

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22734670 . What the paper claims This is an evidence map of 11,628 PubMed-indexed records on generative language models in healthcare, January 2023 to June 2026, built to answer one question: is the clinical literature keeping pace with the systems it evaluates? The central construct is evaluation lag, the number of quarters between the release of the newest model family a study names and that study's own publication quarter. Mean lag widens from 1.33 to 6.08 quarters. Because a discontinued family ages at exactly one quarter per quarter, the authors benchmark that rise against a counterfactual holding 2023 model composition fixed, and find that migration to newer systems offsets 56.2% of the drift (95% CI 49.9-65.2, 2,000 bootstrap resamples). By design, randomised controlled trials evaluate models 4.62 quarters older than other empirical designs (95% CI 3.62-5.63), yet among the records naming a family still receiving releases no design differs from any other; what separates designs is the probability of studying a discontinued family at all, 62.1% for randomised trials against 15.6% for preprints. The framing is right and the execution is unusually careful for a bibliometric paper. Reporting the mechanical ageing rate as the null instead of zero, validating the decomposition by showing that discontinued-only records widen at 1.062 quarters per quarter, and running a pessimistic sensitivity analysis that assumes the earliest release of every named family are all things this literature normally omits. The version-specification result in Section 2 deserves to be read on its own: randomised trials specify the model version in 50.0% of cases, the lowest of any empirical design, which means half of the highest-tier evidence cannot be attributed to a determinate system. My comments below are about three places where the reported precision outruns the design. Does the conclusion hold on the data? 1. Evaluation lag is measured on a differentially selected half of the corpus, and the headline comparison is between designs that differ in exactly that selection. Lag is computable for 5,775 of 11,628 records, and coverage by design runs from 87.0% for comparative evaluations and 69.0% for randomised trials down to 36.2% for preprints and 27.0% for reviews. The paper states this plainly, which is to its credit, but the between-design contrast is its central result and the missingness is both large and design-dependent. The direction is not obvious either: if preprints name a model in the abstract mainly when that model is the novelty on sale, the preprint advantage is inflated; if trials omit the name when the system is an incidental component, the trial penalty may be understated. Two things would settle it. Worst-case bounds in the Manski sense across the plausible range would show whether the ordering survives at all, and a full-text audit of a random sample, a few hundred records stratified by design, would give an empirical estimate of how the non-naming records differ. Without one of those, the contrast rests on an assumption of ignorable missingness that the paper does not state. 2. The abstract quotes the specification that maximises the effect and omits the one that does not survive correction. The median regression gives 4.62 quarters at P = 3.4 x 10^-19; ordinary least squares on the same specification gives an adjusted difference of 1.57 quarters, P = 0.021, and after Holm correction across the seven design contrasts P = 0.084. Median regression is the defensible choice for a strongly right-skewed distribution and the paper says so, so this is not a case of specification shopping. It is a case of a reader meeting one number and not the other. The magnitude differs by a factor of about three between estimators, and the abstract should carry that range, or at minimum state that the estimate

items.summary: Dataset Overview & Methodology This repository provides an experimentally enriched network traffic dataset designed to overcome severe class imbalance in Web attack detection . Focusing on the CICIDS2017 benchmark, which natively contains critically scarce instances for minority Web threats (such as only 21 SQL Injection flows), this dataset incorporates 32,670 authentic attack flows captured in a controlled experimental testbed . Key Characteristics Authentic Capture Environment: Unlike synthetic interpolation methods (e.g., SMOTE) that generate artificial data points within existing boundaries, this dataset captures real network traffic using an Apache XAMPP server and Damn Vulnerable Web Application (DVWA) . It features both automated scripts ( sqlmap , Hydra , Wfuzz ) and manual obfuscation vectors combined with normal background traffic . Feature-Space Consistency: Processed directly via CICFlowMeter to extract the exact 78 statistical flow features required to maintain complete compatibility with the original CICIDS2017 feature space . Rigorously Evaluated Classes: Web SQL Injection (significantly boosted to ensure robust pattern learning) . Web Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) (including reflected and stored variants with filter-evasion techniques) . Web Brute Force (WBF) (generated through multi-day credential-guessing sessions) .

items.summary: emgteach is an open-source Python package that provides a unified PySide6 desktop application for real-time acquisition, offline analysis and maximum voluntary contraction (MVC) normalisation of surface electromyography (sEMG) signals. It is designed for hands-on biopotential acquisition in undergraduate physiology teaching laboratories, and is meant to be set up by instructors with different levels of technical background and used directly by students during a practical session. The application is hardware-agnostic through a common AcquisitionDevice interface and ships with two interchangeable low-cost backends: BITalino (revolution) over Bluetooth, and an Arduino RedBoard Plus + MyoWare 2.0 over USB serial (open firmware included). A single setting switches between them. Main features: Three-tab GUI (Acquisition, Analysis, MVC normalisation) wrapping a reusable, Qt-free analytic core. Bilingual interface (English / Spanish) with automatic start-up language detection and an in-app language switch. Two-channel acquisition (e.g. agonist/antagonist) with a stacked two-channel live view. Automatic contraction-onset detection (baseline + k·SD threshold) stored as EDF+ annotations. Muscle-load analysis (Jonsson APDF): static (P10), median (P50) and peak (P90) %MVC levels, both offline and as a live monitor with warning/danger zones. One-click PDF session and MVC/muscle-load reports. Reliable EDF+ output using a buffered-write pattern that avoids a silent file-corruption artefact during continuous streaming. Reproducible synthetic signals for class assignments and hardware-free continuous integration. Assisted selection of significant fragments, with an editable fragment editor (detection parameters and envelope-filter cut-offs) applied to the analysis. CSV export of results and a live signal-quality check during recording. An ECG signal profile alongside EMG, selectable through a profile registry. Classroom mode: a read-only live dashboard served over the local network so students follow the session on their phone/tablet browser (no install), with a per-session access code so the follower link only works while the broadcast is running. Kinematics via the BITalino accelerometer (v2.0.0): a movement-versus-EMG analysis panel, a guided force-velocity acquisition wizard (an MVC maximum followed by cued quick lifts, each auto-marked with its load), and a force-velocity study that turns one recording into the load-velocity, Hill force-velocity, power and recruitment curves. Since v3.0.0 the accelerometer's input is a stated convention (muscle on A1, accelerometer on A2) rather than a selectable channel. Configuration by practical (v3.0.0): three practicals — one muscle, agonist/antagonist and muscle kinematics — fix the channel count, the accelerometer and what each tab offers, replacing the settings that were previously chosen one at a time. The session as a single file with its phases marked inside it (v3.0.0): warm-up, calibration repetitions, preparation and recording, so the maximum voluntary contraction every percentage is measured against travels with the signal, and a derived (tuned) recording carries the decisions taken on screen. Teaching layer (v3.0.0): a guided tour over the interface, contextual help on every box, one analysis row per contraction with its electromechanical delay, and an agonist/antagonist co-activation index (Falconer-Winter) computed per marked phase in %MVC. Handling at the laboratory bench (v3.1.0): the fragment editor as a three-step procedure that counts the marked contractions against the protocol and lets each be kept, dropped, split or dragged, with the detection sensitivity set per practical and recorded in the report and the CSV; a single running instance with a start-up splash; pictures of the electrode placement and the calibration in the guided tour; and a printable sheet for each station of the agonist/antagonist practical. Patch 3.1.1: the co-activation of a named window is read on the uncut r

items.summary: This white paper examines the commercial cost created when customers question the human care, originality, factual integrity, provenance, or accountability behind AI-assisted brand interactions. It defines this cost as the Authenticity Tax: a cumulative drag on conversion, retention, customer trust, escalation cost, reputational equity, and long-term brand value. Unlike visible rejection or service failure, authenticity-related doubt often remains silent, influencing customer behaviour without producing a clear complaint or attribution signal. The paper identifies six commercial components of the Authenticity Tax: Conversion Drag, Verification Friction, Human Escalation Cost, Correction and Rework, Reputational Discount, and Lost Trust Compounding. It also identifies five structural causes: Provenance Ambiguity, the Effort Discount, the Intentionality Gap, Accountability Diffusion, and Voice Convergence. Together, these mechanisms explain why lower production costs do not automatically translate into higher net value when AI-generated communication reduces customer confidence or perceived care. Case studies covering Air Canada, CNET, and Amazon illustrate three distinct operating patterns. Air Canada demonstrates accountability risk when automated customer guidance conflicts with policy. CNET demonstrates the correction and portfolio-level credibility cost created by weak disclosure and editorial controls. Amazon demonstrates the opposite strategy: investing proactively in authenticity, fraud prevention, review integrity, and trust infrastructure at scale. The paper introduces the Authenticity Proof Stack, comprising Provenance, Accountability, Originality, Contextual Care, Transparency, and Recourse. It also proposes a Human-Care Threshold that matches human involvement to consequence, ranging from AI-first reversible interactions to human-led high-stakes decisions. A Net AI Value equation incorporates Gross Automation Benefit, Authenticity Tax, and Governance Cost to provide a more complete commercial assessment of AI deployment. The central proposition is that authenticity is becoming an operating condition rather than a stylistic brand attribute. In an environment where competent communication becomes abundant, trust increasingly depends on verifiable evidence, visible accountability, original knowledge, appropriate human judgment, and effective recourse.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 4 August 2026.

items.summary: This report documents a controlled lab test, run on 30 March 2026, of whether Automated Moving Target Defense (AMTD) with network deception and inline enforcement contains an autonomous attack agent, and it publishes the per-run logs behind the result. The attacker was an agent built on Microsoft AutoGen (0.2.35) with GPT-4o, told the defense was present, instructed to adapt, and tasked to map a small flat network, read a named target file, and exfiltrate it to a fixed external listener. In a control run with the defense removed, the agent completed the mission in 190 seconds, reaching one internal host and exfiltrating 32,768 bytes, content verified by hash. Across four defended runs with the same agent and environment, the listener recorded zero connections and zero bytes, and the agent reached zero internal hosts; each run was blocked at first contact with a deceptive responder. In the multi-agent run the agent created four fresh identities (one virtual machine and three containers) and each was blocked at its first probe, the virtual-machine identity 178 milliseconds after that probe. The result is scoped deliberately. Four defended runs and one control are a demonstration, not a rate. GPT-4o via AutoGen is a 2024-generation agent shown by a public 2026 evaluation to be weak at long-horizon intrusion, so this test shows containment of that class of agent on a permissive lab network and does not establish containment of a current frontier agent. The defense ran as a full production stack; the logs show rotation was active and that blocked probes struck rotating deceptive surfaces, but isolating rotation from deception requires an ablation not run here. The evidence package (sensor export, agent tool log, listener log, clock provenance, SHA-256 manifest) is released with the report. This is the empirical companion to the author's architectural preprint (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21347479).
